name: housing
prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: a production-ready modular hand-painted interface housing for Endsieg, a historical strategy game with the visual craft of vanilla Hearts of Iron IV. Create ONE blank square instrument casing inspired by 1914–1940 military field-radio and telegraph equipment. This is a reusable GUI frame component, not a whole radio or a mockup screen. Composition: strict straight-on orthographic front view, perfectly aligned horizontal/vertical edges, square proportions, casing fills 94 percent of the canvas with even margin, transparent background outside. Materials: substantial hammered charcoal cast-steel perimeter approximately 10 percent of total width, softly rounded outer corners, black-brown Bakelite inner collar, subdued machined nickel/chrome lip, four countersunk slotted screws in fixed corners. Central opening occupies roughly 76 percent of width and height and is filled with quiet near-black matte enamel; it must remain flat and blank for readable in-game text. Broad bevels with warm gray upper-left highlights and deep contact shadows, period wear only at edges, high-quality painted game-interface art with convincing physical material, restrained contrast. Edges must be continuous and usable in a nine-slice scalable frame. No attached knobs, no needles, no dials, no gauges, no switches, no logos, flags, emblems, icons, letters, numbers or any text. No perspective, no modern glossy touchscreen styling, no environment or table, no vignette or detached cast shadow. A single physical empty housing with transparent exterior.

name: push_key
prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: a single production-ready reusable push-key component for Endsieg, a 1910–1945 historical strategy game with Paradox-style hand-painted interface art. Create ONE wide rectangular mechanical command key inspired by a military field-telephone switchboard or radio-control panel. Strict orthographic front view, no perspective. A horizontal key with width-to-height ratio about 4:1 centered in a transparent canvas, fills almost the entire canvas width, generous but even transparent margin. Solid black-brown Bakelite push-cap with a gently convex domed face; substantial dark cast-steel socket and a worn nickel/chrome retaining bezel. Slightly clipped rounded corners, convincing raised mechanical depth, subtle upper-left metal highlights and lower contact shadow within the socket. Wide completely blank center surface for an in-game text label; no text, letters, numbers, symbols, icons, logos, gauges, lights, additional buttons, scale marks or objects. Match the material character of 1914–1940 military communications equipment: aged brown-black phenolic material, warm gray dark iron, restrained dull silver accents, tiny edge scuffs, elegant readable game art, not photorealistic product advertising. No attached screw ornaments on the central push-cap. Edge pieces must remain clean enough for horizontally scalable game buttons. Transparent outside only, opaque key cap and housing. One single blank mechanical push-key, no grid or presentation board.
